findings.title: #938 AC2: the Needs-you surface never names the bill
findings.evidence: AC2: "The Accruals page AND NEEDS YOU render the item with the accrual, THE BILL and the period named". apps/web/components/firm/accrual-bill-conflict-affordance.tsx (98 lines, the whole file) renders only an ErrorMessage, the skip-reason Input and the two Buttons — it contains no Link, no href and no reference to row.entry_id or row.document_id (grep for 'Link|href|entry' matches one comment line). The generic renderer apps/web/components/firm/needs-you-row.tsx renders question_text (line 149), amount_cents (168-171) and period (174-177) and never entry_id. Only apps/web/components/accruals/accrual-bill-conflicts.tsx:108-111 builds the 'View the bill' link (journalEntryHref). The ticket report wave4-lane03-ticket938.md asserts under AC2 that 'Both name the accrual (question_text), the bill (entry_id -> "View the bill" link) and the period' — that claim is true of the Accruals page only.
findings.required_fix: Render the bill on the Needs-you row for this kind — a journalEntryHref link from row.entry_id inside AccrualBillConflictAffordance is the smallest honest change — or record the gap explicitly and correct the AC2 claim in the ticket report.

findings.title: #942 AC3: an ISSUED invoice posted through the trade-invoice lane can never surface
findings.evidence: AC3: "an ISSUED INVOICE or receipt posting to the accrual's revenue account inside a posted, un-reversed period surfaces with the same two remedies". The read admits only document-filed entries: packages/db/migrations/0302_accrual_bill_conflict.sql:322 `and je.status='approved' and je.origin='document' and je.document_id is not null`, and 0304 splices only the side key and the sentence, never the predicate. A sales invoice admitted through the trade-invoice lane posts through clara._record_journal_entry_core (packages/db/migrations/0225_trade_invoices.sql:1844-1847, re-read live from pg_get_functiondef on clara_l03): `insert into clara.journal_entries(client_id,status,posting_date,memo,origin,maker_actor,flags) values (...,'agent',clara.agent_user_id(),...)` — origin='agent', document_id never set, and trade_invoices.kind admits 'sales_invoice' with a NULLABLE source_document_id. Such an invoice therefore double-counts the period's revenue against the un-reversed accrual with no warning. The only cell for this arm, p942.conflict (packages/db/tests/accrual-revenue-side.test.mjs:452-474), drives postedDocumentEntry — the filed-document route — exclusively. (#938's own AC1 says 'document-sourced journal entries', so the expense side is within its words; #942's AC3 widened the wording and the implementation did not follow.)
findings.required_fix: Either widen the predicate to reach agent/Work-admitted entries on the accrual's P&L leg (with a cell driving admit_trade_invoice for a sales_invoice), or state in the ticket and in packages/db/README.md's 0304 section that AC3 covers the filed-document route only and file the residual.

findings.title: #938 AC3: no cell proves "each remedy leaves exactly one live expense for the period"
findings.evidence: AC3: "Cells: same-period bill surfaces the item; next-period bill does not; EACH REMEDY LEAVES EXACTLY ONE LIVE EXPENSE FOR THE PERIOD AFTERWARDS; from-scratch apply." packages/db/tests/accrual-bill-conflict.test.mjs has nine cells (p938.read.same_period, .next_period, .different_account, .reverse_clears, p938.reverse_now.refuses_when_not_due, p938.skip.blocks_scan, .refusals, .idempotent, p938.role_floor); none reads clara.journal_lines or sums an account (grep for journal_lines returns nothing). The row clearing is asserted; the ledger arithmetic is not. The report itself names this under AC3 and under 'Anything unverified'. Note that #942 DID write the equivalent assertion on the revenue side (p942.posts, netOnAccount over journal_lines, accrual-revenue-side.test.mjs:262-281), so the shape exists in the lane and was simply not applied to #938's own AC.
findings.required_fix: Add one cell per remedy that sums clara.journal_lines on the accrual's P&L account for the flagged period after the act and asserts it equals the bill alone (reuse accrual-revenue-side.test.mjs's netOnAccount helper).

findings.title: #938 AC1: the read collapses to one row per plan, and the shared-file comment describes the opposite tie-break
findings.evidence: AC1 asks for a read that "LISTS ... document-sourced journal ENTRIES". packages/db/migrations/0302_accrual_bill_conflict.sql:299 uses `select distinct on (o.plan_id)` with `order by o.plan_id,o.due_date,je.posting_date,je.id` (line 339) — at most one row per plan, tie broken on the EARLIEST due date, which the migration header states outright (line 48-49: "AT MOST ONE ROW PER PLAN ... ties break on the earliest due date"). The grounding comment added to the shared file apps/web/lib/firm/needs-you.ts:166-168 says the opposite: "ONE row per accrual PLAN ... whose MOST RECENT posted, unreversed accrual occurrence has a document-sourced ... entry". A quarterly plan with two open occurrences, or one period carrying two bills, surfaces one row naming the earliest — not what the comment tells the next reader.
findings.required_fix: Correct the needs-you.ts comment to 'the earliest posted, unreversed occurrence' (ADDITIVE edit inside the existing block, per the lane's shared-file rule), or change the ordering to match the comment and re-measure.

findings.title: #938 AC1: the document-service-period route is implemented but uncelled
findings.evidence: AC1: "whose posting date (OR THE DOCUMENT'S SERVICE PERIOD WHEN ONE IS RECORDED) falls inside an occurrence". The branch exists — 0302:328-331, the `or exists (select 1 from clara.document_service_periods dsp ... dsp.period_start<=pw.period_end and dsp.period_end>=o.period_key)` arm, guarded by 0302:151's to_regclass check. Every cell in accrual-bill-conflict.test.mjs drives the posting_date route; none records a service period. The report names this as a follow-up. The fixture is already to hand (accrual-adjustments-fixtures.mjs's filedDocumentWithTerm).
findings.required_fix: One cell: a bill whose posting_date falls OUTSIDE the accrued period but whose recorded service period overlaps it must surface; the same bill with a superseded service period must not.

findings.title: #942 AC2: the Accruals-page bill-conflict copy is expense-only on both sides

findings.title: #937 AC3: the final-period remainder rule governs only an even split
findings.evidence: The ticket body: "the stated amounts must sum EXACTLY to the accrual's total, WITH ANY CENT REMAINDER PLACED IN THE FINAL PERIOD (the prepayment lane's `final_period` rule)". The implementation makes the exact-sum rule law and the remainder a wall over exactly the shape it can govern — a set that IS an equal split with one odd period must place the odd period last; a genuinely uneven set (July 3,000 / August 3,500) never enters the arm. Cells pin the boundary in both directions (p937.walls.uneven; '937.periods: the final-period remainder governs an EVEN split and nothing else'). The report flags this as its own judgement call, and the ticket lists it among 'decisions taken with defaults the owner may flip on review'.
findings.required_fix: None mandatory: put the reading to the owner at the next grill, since the ticket's two halves cannot both be literal. Keep the two cells that pin the boundary.

findings.title: #942: a correction landing between a posted accrual and its reversal strands the difference (measured, pre-existing, correctly deferred)
findings.evidence: The report's follow-up 2, measured in this lane: an accrual admitted at 300,000 posts 300,000; a correction to 275,000 revises the plan; the reversal admitted afterwards is built from the LIVE revision's basis and posts 275,000, leaving 25,000 on the balance-sheet leg permanently. It is identical on the expense side (0193's reversal basis plus #936's correction door), so it is not caused by #942 and is nobody's acceptance criterion. p942.correct deliberately asserts the SIDE of every leg rather than blessing the amounts.

summary: Three tickets, fifteen findings, no blocker. Every acceptance criterion outside the frozen conversation half is built and driven through real doors, and the three database batteries plus the lane's web cells were re-run here and are green (9/9, 12/12, 8/8, 90/90). Three findings are majors and all three are about an AC clause that the implementation narrows without saying so on the surface: #938's Needs-you item never names the bill AC2 asks for; #938 has no cell for AC3's 'exactly one live expense' although #942 wrote exactly that assertion for the revenue side; and #942's AC3 revenue arm can only ever see filed-document entries, so an issued sales invoice posted through the trade-invoice lane (origin='agent', no document_id) double-counts the period's revenue unwarned. The rest are narrowings the reports themselves flag (the remainder rule's scope, the service-period route's missing cell, zh), copy that is expense-flavoured on both sides, one shared-file comment that describes the opposite tie-break from the SQL, and one overstated 'nothing like this exists' measurement. The successor contracts for the chatTurn_v22 cut are present, specific and correctly deferred.
